raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`TRTLLMMLABackend` calls flashinfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` once per prefix chunk and once for the causal pass of every MLA layer in an eager prefill. Before launching, flashinfer (≥ 0.6.18, including the 0.7.0.post1 pinned on main) checks for empty rows. Without host lengths it reads them off the device:

```python
has_inactive_rows = bool((~active_rows).any().item())   # D2H copy + stream sync
```

sglang never passes `q_seq_lens_cpu` / `kv_seq_lens_cpu`, so every call blocks the host until the GPU drains, and the GPU then idles while the host relaunches. Both lengths already exist on the host: `extend_seq_lens_cpu` and `prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu`.

## Modifications

- `TRTLLMMLAPrefillMetadata.host_seq_lens`: an int32 CPU copy of `extend_seq_lens_cpu` and its sum, built once per forward. The prefix-chunk lengths and totals come from the existing `prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu` / `prefix_chunk_num_tokens` (None-checked).
- `_run_prefill_kernel` takes optional `q_seq_lens_cpu` / `kv_seq_lens_cpu` and forwards them to flashinfer. `TokenspeedMLABackend`'s override accepts them.
- Both ragged call sites go through `_host_seq_lens`, which passes the lengths only when they cover q/k exactly and no graph is being captured. Otherwise the stock call runs.

There is no new flag. flashinfer makes the same empty-row decision from the same values, so the same kernel launches on the same inputs.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, `--attention-backend trtllm_mla --disable-prefill-cuda-graph`, which routes every extend through the ragged kernel. 2 boots per arm, 1×GB300.

| | main (2 boots) | this PR (2 boots) |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot) | 0.654 / 0.657 | 0.660 / 0.660 |
| greedy outputs, 32 prompts (short and 19.8k shared-prefix) | identical across all 6 boot pairs | identical across all 6 boot pairs |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Profile** (same setup, 2 requests with a cached 19.8k prefix):

| | ragged calls | `cudaStreamSynchronize` |
|---|---|---|
| main | 108 | 108 (all inside the ragged call) |
| this PR | 108 | **0** |

**bench_serving**, 1×GB300, one arm at a time in off/on/on/off order. Each cell lists the individual runs, then the change in means.

| workload | prefill graph | input tok/s: main → PR | mean TTFT (ms): main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| random-ids 8k in / 16 out, conc 8 | default | 77,721, 78,406 → 86,986, 84,415 (**+9.8%**) | 631, 617 → 493, 535 (**−17.6%**) |
| random-ids 32k in / 16 out, conc 4 | default | 54,521\*, 71,363 → 70,932, 74,409 (**+1.8%** vs the second main run) | 1,982\*, 1,416 → 1,326, 1,271 (**−8.3%**) |
| generated-shared-prefix 16k + 512, conc 16 | disabled | 205,567, 205,966 → 212,733, 211,137 (**+3.0%**) | 978, 982 → 965, 859 (**−7.0%**) |

\* The first long-prompt run after the pod started; it is an outlier and is excluded from the 32k means. In an earlier round of the same A/B, main read 69,263 and 72,701 tok/s on this workload.

With the default breakable prefill CUDA graph, extends of 2,048 tokens or fewer run in-graph, where trtllm_mla falls back to FlashInfer, so the change only affects longer (eager) prefills.

Tested on v0.5.21 (the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` image; main needs sglang-kernel ≥ 0.4.9). The diff applies to v0.5.21 unchanged, and the code it touches is the same on main.

## Checklist


- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Unit test added: `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_trtllm_mla_ragged_host_seq_lens.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`).
- [x] No documentation change needed (no new flag).
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.
- [x] Follows the code-style guide.

+
+
+def _prefix_chunk_host_seq_lens(forward_batch, chunk_idx):
+    if (
+        forward_batch.prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu is None
+        or forward_batch.prefix_chunk_num_tokens is None
+    ):
+        return None
+    return HostSeqLens(
+        lens=forward_batch.prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu[chunk_idx],
+        total=forward_batch.prefix_chunk_num_tokens[chunk_idx],
+    )
+
+
+def _host_seq_lens(q, k, q_lens, kv_lens):
+    """Host q/kv lengths let flashinfer skip its empty-row .item() sync. Pass
+    them only when they cover q/k exactly and no graph is being captured."""
+    if (
+        q_lens is None
+        or kv_lens is None
+        or q_lens.total != q.shape[0]
+        or kv_lens.total != k.shape[0]
+        or (torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing())
+    ):
+        return {}
+    return {"q_seq_lens_cpu": q_lens.lens, "kv_seq_lens_cpu": kv_lens.lens}

@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+"""trtllm_mla passes host q/kv lengths to flashinfer's ragged prefill. CPU-only."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention import trtllm_mla_backend
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.trtllm_mla_backend import (
+    HostSeqLens,
+    TRTLLMMLABackend,
+    _host_seq_lens,
+    _prefix_chunk_host_seq_lens,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _lens(*values):
+    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int32)
+
+
+def _host(*values):
+    return HostSeqLens(lens=_lens(*values), total=sum(values))
+
+
+class TestHostSeqLens(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_passes_lens_that_cover_q_and_k(self):
+        q_lens, kv_lens = _host(3, 5), _host(0, 7)
+        kwargs = _host_seq_lens(torch.empty(8, 2), torch.empty(7, 2), q_lens, kv_lens)
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["q_seq_lens_cpu"], q_lens.lens)
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["kv_seq_lens_cpu"], kv_lens.lens)
+
+    def test_stock_call_on_padding_or_missing_lens(self):
+        q, k = torch.empty(8, 2), torch.empty(7, 2)
+        for args in (
+            (torch.empty(16, 2), k, _host(3, 5), _host(4, 3)),  # padded q
+            (q, torch.empty(16, 2), _host(3, 5), _host(4, 3)),  # padded k
+            (q, k, None, _host(4, 3)),
+            (q, k, _host(3, 5), None),
+        ):
+            self.assertEqual(_host_seq_lens(*args), {})
+
+    def test_prefix_chunk_lens(self):
+        lens = torch.tensor([[4, 3], [0, 2]], dtype=torch.int32)
+        fb = SimpleNamespace(
+            prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu=lens, prefix_chunk_num_tokens=[7, 2]
+        )
+        chunk = _prefix_chunk_host_seq_lens(fb, 1)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(chunk.lens, lens[1]))
+        self.assertEqual(chunk.total, 2)
+        unset = SimpleNamespace(
+            prefix_chunk_seq_lens_cpu=None, prefix_chunk_num_tokens=None
+        )
+        self.assertIsNone(_prefix_chunk_host_seq_lens(unset, 0))
+
+    def test_run_prefill_kernel_forwards_lens(self):
+        received = {}
+
+        def fake_ragged(**kwargs):
+            received.update(kwargs)
+            return kwargs["out"]
+
+        backend = TRTLLMMLABackend.__new__(TRTLLMMLABackend)
+        backend.data_type = torch.bfloat16
+        backend.workspace_buffer = torch.empty(16, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        q = torch.zeros(8, 2, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        lens = _lens(3, 5)
+        # flashinfer is imported only on CUDA builds.
+        fake_flashinfer = SimpleNamespace(
+            prefill=SimpleNamespace(trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek=fake_ragged)
+        )
+        with patch.object(
+            trtllm_mla_backend, "flashinfer", fake_flashinfer, create=True
+        ):
+            backend._run_prefill_kernel(
+                q=q,
+                k=q,
+                v=q,
+                layer=SimpleNamespace(scaling=1.0),
+                batch_size=2,
+                cum_seq_lens_q=_lens(0, 3, 8),
+                max_q_len=5,
+                seq_lens_kv=lens,
+                cum_seq_lens_kv=_lens(0, 3, 8),
+                max_kv_len=5,
+                is_causal=True,
+                return_lse=False,
+                out_buffer=torch.empty_like(q),
+                q_seq_lens_cpu=lens,
+                kv_seq_lens_cpu=lens,
+            )
+        self.assertIs(received["q_seq_lens_cpu"], lens)
+        self.assertIs(received["kv_seq_lens_cpu"], lens)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
